stance_summary: The dated mechanism is Australian housing transmission, not a valuation that AONIA is 'too high'. Verified: overnight AONIA 4.35 on 17-Sep-2026; ASX 30-day AONIA_2026-10 implied 4.565 (+21.5bp) with 21752 open interest; Nov 4.685 / Dec 4.725; Mar-2027 terminal 4.86 (+51bp); NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% YoY and transaction volumes -18% with Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak (16-Sep-2026); AU inflation gauge 82 vs labor 50 / consumer 48 / activity 54; AU 2Y 4.999, 99.0th 1y percentile, +39.1bp 1m. Inference: the next RBA decision must confront a working housing channel, so the discrete October hike premium should reprice lower even if inflation stays hot. Unknown: exact next RBA date is not in the packet; whether the next CPI confirms the 82-gauge; whether WTI 107.02 / Brent 130.80 (96th/99.6th percentiles, as-of 15-Sep-2026) overwhelm housing. Rates beat spot because AONIA_2026-10 is the meeting contract; AUDUSD 0.712 can stay bid on commodities.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Long AONIA_2026-10 (receive Oct-26 ASX 30-day AONIA / short implied cash rate) at packet implied 4.565 versus overnight AONIA 4.35; Nov 4.685 and Dec 4.725 are the adjacent hike-path contracts.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short AUDUSD from packet mid 0.712022 (as-of 2026-09-18; 1y percentile 76.4, 5y percentile 84.3).
expression_comparison.rationale: The mispricing is a discrete next-meeting hike already in AONIA_2026-10 (+21.5bp, most liquid AONIA contract). That contract is the settlement mechanism for the RBA hold-vs-hike event. AUDUSD can remain bid on copper/energy and CFTC leveraged-fund AUD longs even if the RBA holds, so spot is a noisier expression of the same housing-to-policy path. Rates are comparably clean and are the default.

context_build.causal_mechanism: RBA cash-rate tightening is now reducing housing turnover and collateral values. That transmission constraint should cap further near-term hikes even while the inflation gauge remains hot, so the October AONIA contract that already prices a 21.5bp move from overnight AONIA should reprice lower at the next RBA decision and housing/CPI prints.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Overnight AONIA is 4.35 (17-Sep-2026). The Sep-26 30-day contract is 4.355 (+0.5bp). The Oct-26 contract jumps to 4.565 (+21.5bp) with 4450 volume, then Nov 4.685 (+33.5bp) and Dec 4.725 (+37.5bp); policy-path terminal is Mar-2027 at 4.86 (+51bp). AU 2Y is 4.999 as-of 16-Sep-2026 after a +39.1bp 1-month rise (1y percentile 99.0, 5y percentile 99.8). AU 2s10s is +34.9bp and flattened 13.0bp over 1m. AUDUSD is 0.712 after +2.65% over 3m. Desk thesis on the same cutoff: energy shock is constraining the global easing impulse; the AU-specific overlay is that housing has already broken.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: AU inflation gauge 82 and a global energy shock (WTI 107.02, Brent 130.80, 15-Sep-2026) that already justify some additional RBA tightening, which is why Oct-Dec AONIA prices 21.5-37.5bp of hikes. New as-of 16-Sep-2026: NSW stamp-duty receipts down 24% YoY, volumes down 18%, Sydney and Melbourne values more than 7% below peak — evidence the tightening channel is biting now, not in prospect. That housing print is the information that should change the next meeting, not a restatement of the 82 inflation score.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: AONIA_2026-10 at 4.565 assumes the RBA delivers about 21.5bp of additional tightening in the October window versus overnight AONIA 4.35, with another ~16bp into year-end (Dec 4.725) and a Mar-2027 terminal of 4.86. That path treats inflation/energy as still dominant over housing transmission.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: The October hike is not the base case once housing turnover and prices are already contracting at pandemic-scale stamp-duty rates. Inflation 82 can stay high without the RBA delivering the first 21.5bp already in AONIA_2026-10.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level: AONIA 4.35 overnight versus Oct implied 4.565, Nov 4.685, Dec 4.725, Mar-2027 4.86; AU 2Y 4.999. Change: the entire near-term hike is in the Sep-to-Oct AONIA step (+21.0bp contract-to-contract) rather than a slow grind; AU 2Y +16.4bp 5d and +39.1bp 1m, with a -5.5bp 1d fade on 16-Sep-2026. Marginal driver of the rates expression is the next-meeting cash-rate assumption in the Oct 30-day contract, not term premium in 10s (AU 10Y analog lives on a 12-day-stale max-age gauge).

AONIA Oct is +21.5bp versus overnight, the largest single front-month step on the live 30-day strip. AU 2s10s 34.9bp is 24.4th 1y percentile after a 13.0bp 1m flattening. AUDUSD 1y percentile 76.4 is elevated, not a 1y extreme; AUDNZD is a 99.8th 1y/5y extreme.
analogs: AU 2Y 1m +39.1bp analog 2022-09-28 (prior 1m +39.2bp, level 3.572): forward 1m -37.4bp and forward 3m -15.0bp after a similar backup during RBA tightening.
AU 2Y analog 2025-12-22 (prior 1m +39.0bp, level 4.078): forward 1m +8.8bp and forward 3m +54.7bp, i.e. the backup continued.

historical_reference.regime_differences: 2022-09-28 occurred as pandemic inflation was rolling over and oil was off the war spike; 2026 still has AU inflation gauge 82, WTI/Brent at 96th/99.6th percentiles, and a desk thesis that the energy shock is blocking global easing. Housing has already fallen more than 7% from peak, which is later in the transmission sequence than early-2022. Packet does not date the next RBA meeting, so analog calendars cannot be matched 1:1.

trade.structure: Long AONIA_2026-10 in implied-rate space (ASX 30-day AONIA). Paper side long profits if the implied cash rate falls (receive RBA path). Trusted code marks tradable_rate_curves.AONIA 2026-10 implied_rate.
trade.thesis: FACT: Housing is already contracting on 16-Sep-2026 data while AONIA_2026-10 still prices 4.565 versus overnight 4.35. FACT: AU inflation gauge is 82 and oil is at a 1y extreme, which is the reason that hike is in the strip. INFERENCE: The next RBA decision is the dated repricing event for that 21.5bp; a hold or a housing-weighted statement should collapse Oct toward overnight rather than toward Nov 4.685. INFERENCE: 2022-09-28 is the comparable AU 2Y backup that subsequently rallied 37.4bp in 1m, but 2023-05-10 and 2025-12-22 show same-size backups that continued. UNKNOWN: meeting date, next CPI, and whether energy keeps the RBA on the 4.86 Mar-2027 terminal. This seat rejects waiting for AU 2Y mean reversion without that meeting/data path.
trade.mispricing: AONIA_2026-10 implied 4.565 prices a near-full extra hike in the next cash-rate window after evidence that the housing channel is already biting. That is a meeting-path error, not a claim that 4.999 2Y is rich on percentile alone.
why_now: 16-Sep-2026 housing print (stamp duty -24% YoY, volumes -18%, values more than 7% below peak) is new versus the already-known 82 inflation gauge.
AONIA_2026-10 still sits +21.5bp through the freeze at 20-Sep-2026T02:08:18Z, so the meeting premium has not been pulled.
Global energy shock is the competing catalyst; the AU-specific override has to be expressed before the next RBA statement, not after.
Sidecar open_positions is empty, so this is a fresh OPEN versus the $100m gross cap and 3.85% SOFR vig (effective 17-Sep-2026).
evidence_refs: rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
trade.horizon: 2-6 weeks, into the next RBA decision and the next AU housing/CPI prints
trade.entry: Packet mid AONIA_2026-10 implied_rate 4.565 (ASX 30-day, tradable_rate_curves; price 95.435). Do not invent a broker quote.
trade.target: Repricing toward overnight AONIA 4.35 (17-Sep-2026 benchmark) if the October hike is not delivered; adjacent Nov implied 4.685 is the path that should cheapen with it.
trade.invalidation: Next RBA decision hikes, or AONIA_2026-10 implied rate rises through the packet Nov contract 4.685, confirming inflation/energy still dominate housing transmission.
catalysts: Next RBA cash-rate decision and statement language on housing versus inflation.
Subsequent Australian housing turnover/prices and CPI prints that either validate the 16-Sep-2026 downturn or re-accelerate inflation from gauge 82.
Oil follow-through after the 16-Sep-2026 Saudi Oman workaround (WTI/Brent still 107.02/130.80 as-of 15-Sep-2026) if energy re-widens the hike path.
principal_risks: Inflation gauge 82 plus WTI/Brent 96th/99.6th percentiles can force the RBA to deliver the Oct hike regardless of stamp duty.
2023-05-10 and 2025-12-22 AU 2Y analogs continued higher after a similar +39bp 1m backup.
Exact next RBA date is unknown in the packet, so the Oct contract can roll without a hold.
Bank-bill-minus-OIS is cross-vintage unavailable; 6m bank bill 5.07 sits above the AONIA strip and may already discount more tightening.
AUD leveraged-fund length does not hedge an AONIA long if the meeting hawks and AUD still holds.

remit: credible path from mispricing to repricing
